from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Signals are combinations of simple waves.",
            "Time domain shows when signals occur.",
            "Frequency domain shows contained pitches.",
            "Fourier transforms bridge both domains.",
            "Music notes illustrate this duality."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Intuition: The Fourier Perspective", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements
        wave = FunctionGraph(lambda x: np.sin(x*3), color=WHITE)
        spectral_lines = VGroup(*[Line(UP*0.5, DOWN*0.5, color=YELLOW).shift(RIGHT*i*0.5) for i in range(4)])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#ADD8E6")
        title_fourier = Text("Fourier Perspective", color="#ADD8E6", font_size=32)
        self.place_at_grid(title_fourier, 'A3')
        self.play(FadeIn(title_fourier))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.place_in_area(wave, 'B2', 'C5', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(wave))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.play(FadeOut(wave), FadeIn(self.place_at_grid(spectral_lines, 'C3')))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#00FF00")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#FF69B4")
        self.wait(1)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Core Concept: Narrow vs. Broad", [
            "Narrowing in time spreads frequency.",
            "Spreading in time narrows frequency.",
            "This is a fundamental trade-off."
        ])
        
        # Visuals
        time_pulse = self.place_in_area(
            VGroup(
                Line(LEFT, RIGHT, color=WHITE),
                Polygon(ORIGIN, 0.2*UP, 0.4*RIGHT, 0.2*DOWN, color="#90EE90", fill_opacity=1)
            ),
            'A1', 'C3', scale_factor=1.0
        )
        freq_spread = self.place_in_area(
            VGroup(
                Line(LEFT, RIGHT, color=WHITE),
                Rectangle(height=0.3, width=1.5, color="#FFA500", fill_opacity=0.7)
            ),
            'D1', 'F3', scale_factor=1.0
        )
        broad_pulse = self.place_in_area(
            VGroup(
                Line(LEFT, RIGHT, color=WHITE),
                Rectangle(height=0.2, width=1.8, color="#FF77FF", fill_opacity=0.7)
            ),
            'A4', 'C6', scale_factor=1.0
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#90EE90"), FadeIn(time_pulse))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFA500"), FadeIn(freq_spread))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF77FF"), FadeIn(broad_pulse))

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Uncertainty follows Heisenberg-Gabor inequality.",
            "Signal product has a minimum floor.",
            "We cannot shrink both windows simultaneously.",
            "Pushing time forces frequency expansion.",
            "Wave math limits precision boundaries."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Mathematical Bound", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define elements
        ineq_symbol = MathTex(r"\geq", color="#E0FFFF")
        formula = MathTex(r"\Delta t \cdot \Delta f \geq \frac{1}{4\pi}", color="#FFFFFF")
        
        self.place_at_grid(ineq_symbol, 'C3', scale_factor=3.0)
        self.place_at_grid(formula, 'C3', scale_factor=1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(ineq_symbol), self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#E0FFFF"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(formula), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#FF6347"))
        self.play(Indicate(formula, color=WHITE))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#98FB98"))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Real-World Application: The Bat's Chirp", [
            "Bats balance precision via sonar.",
            "Short clicks improve timing resolution.",
            "Long whistles improve frequency resolution."
        ])
        
        # Animations
        # Define shapes
        bat_wave = FunctionGraph(lambda t: np.sin(2 * np.pi * 5 * t) * np.exp(-t**2), x_range=[-2, 2])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)
        wave = FunctionGraph(lambda t: 0.5 * np.sin(5 * np.pi * t), x_range=[-2, 2]).set_color(WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(wave, 'B2', 'C5')
        self.play(Create(wave))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(GREEN)
        # Short click: high freq, short duration
        click = FunctionGraph(lambda t: 0.5 * np.sin(20 * np.pi * t) * np.exp(-5*t**2), x_range=[-1, 1], color=GREEN)
        self.place_in_area(click, 'D2', 'E2')
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(wave, click))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        # Long whistle: low freq, long duration
        whistle = FunctionGraph(lambda t: 0.5 * np.sin(2 * np.pi * t) * np.exp(-0.5*t**2), x_range=[-2, 2], color=YELLOW)
        self.place_in_area(whistle, 'D4', 'E6')
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(click, whistle))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary and Synthesis", [
            "Uncertainty is a wave property.",
            "Optimal windows define signal processing.",
            "Engineering requires balancing these trade-offs."
        ])
        
        # Elements
        pulse = Dot(color=BLUE)
        freq_label = Text("Pulse-Freq Relation", font_size=20, color=BLUE)
        fundamental_bound = Text("Δt * Δf ≥ K", font_size=36, color=WHITE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.place_at_grid(pulse, "B2")
        self.place_at_grid(freq_label, "B4")
        self.play(FadeIn(pulse), Write(freq_label))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.place_at_grid(fundamental_bound, "D3")
        self.play(FadeIn(fundamental_bound))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(GREEN)
        self.play(FadeOut(pulse), FadeOut(freq_label), FadeOut(fundamental_bound), FadeOut(self.lecture), FadeOut(self.title))

outline.topic: The Uncertainty Principle: The Duality of Time and Frequency

sections.title: Prerequisite Intuition: The Fourier Perspective
sections.content: Briefly define a signal as a combination of simple waves (sines/cosines). Introduce the two domains: Time (when it happens) and Frequency (what notes it contains). Establish that the Fourier Transform is the bridge between them.
sections.example: Visualize a music box: The 'Time' domain shows the sequence of notes being played; the 'Frequency' domain shows the sheet music notation of the specific pitches.

sections.title: The Core Concept: Narrow vs. Broad
sections.content: Explain that 'narrowing' a signal in one domain necessarily 'spreads' it in the other. Use a graphical representation showing a tall, thin spike in the time domain becoming a flat, wide plateau in the frequency domain.
sections.example: Imagine a camera shutter: If you take a photo with a 'narrow' exposure time (a blink), you capture the 'where' but lose the motion information (frequency) of the subject.

sections.title: The Mathematical Bound
sections.content: Introduce the Heisenberg-Gabor Inequality: Δt · Δf ≥ 1/(4π). Explain that we cannot shrink both uncertainty windows simultaneously. The product has a hard floor—a limit imposed by the nature of wave math.
sections.example: An animated 'energy box' that cannot be squeezed smaller than a fixed area; pushing the sides in (time) forces the top and bottom to expand (frequency).

sections.title: Real-World Application: The Bat's Chirp
sections.content: Demonstrate why this matters. A bat needs to locate prey (timing) but also identify prey type (frequency). Explain the trade-off bats make in their sonar pulses to balance precision in both domains.
sections.example: Show a bat emitting a 'Short Click' (Great time resolution, poor frequency resolution) vs. a 'Long Whistle' (Great frequency resolution, poor time resolution) as they approach an insect.

sections.title: Summary and Synthesis
sections.content: Recap that the Uncertainty Principle isn't a flaw in our instruments, but a fundamental property of waves. Conclude with the importance of 'Optimal Windows' in signal processing.
sections.example: The 'Signal Engineering Seesaw': Balancing the time-frequency trade-off to get the best of both worlds for radar, music, and quantum mechanics.
